name: Priyanshu Yogi
headline: Forward Deployed Engineer | Enterprise AI from the discovery call to a system that runs on site | I build agents and publish the evals, misses included

hero.headline: Don't read my resume. Talk to it.
hero.subtext: Economics and political science, then self-taught software engineering, enterprise AI products, a lot of time with customers, and now agents, RAG and voice. Ask my AI about any of it.
hero.motif: Human systems → software systems → intelligent systems

brandIdea: I like understanding systems, then building them.
summary: Forward deployed engineer who takes enterprise AI from the discovery call to a system running on site: architecture, PoC, integration, deployment and the debugging after. At HawkVision AI, ran 12 PoCs across 50+ enterprise computer-vision opportunities in 7 countries. Now building LLM agents with published evals, misses included.
philosophy: The best technical solution is not merely the most sophisticated one. It is the one that survives contact with users, infrastructure, commercial constraints, and deployment reality.

positioning.oneLiner: I learned to think about human systems first, then taught myself how to build technical systems.
positioning.currentDirection: Between roles since leaving HawkVision in August 2026, and available immediately, remote or on-site. Building LLM agents in public meanwhile, with the evals published, misses included.
positioning.lookingFor: Building technically difficult products that solve real user problems, at the intersection of engineering, customers and product.

currentlyBuilding: SignalRoom, a grounded discovery-to-brief workflow with a published evaluation (working demo, synthetic data only)
ReadTrail, a privacy-first Chrome reading companion with a Desk for writing beside saved passages (working MVP; 2.0 on GitHub, not yet on the Chrome Web Store)
This portfolio: a voice-capable AI agent grounded in structured profile data
Experiments: Cochlea, a vocal-analysis MCP server heading toward a coach for beginner singers (in progress); Spotify Mood Curator (working MVP); Atlas, a personal capture pipeline (in progress)

evidence.text: Built frontend dashboards, backend APIs and Computer Vision pipeline integrations on HawkVision's core engineering team; used Terraform for deployment pipelines.
Built Instipe, a NestJS/GraphQL payment system for educational institutions processing 50+ lakh INR/month; cut a GraphQL query from 10+ seconds to under 100ms.
Led a 5-engineer team shipping Hazo (NestJS, React Native, AWS) and WorkOS.

ReadTrail: a Manifest V3 Chrome extension with a canvas reading guide, a side panel and a writing Desk, every message validated at one service-worker trust boundary, 394 unit and behavioral tests and 11 Playwright end-to-end scenarios.
SignalRoom: FastAPI and LangGraph with a SQLite checkpointer, strict-schema structured output recorded and replayed by content hash, and an evaluation suite that runs in CI without a key.

Kept the portfolio's agent answering when a provider withdrew the free model it ran on, by routing across four OpenAI-compatible providers with a circuit breaker and a prompt sized to each one's token budget.

Spotify Mood Curator: Claude proposes songs, the listener's own Spotify data labels them, and a verify step checks what was saved against the plan. Two live CLI runs saved 25 of 25 and 30 of 30 songs in planned order with no duplicates.
Solutioned 50+ enterprise Computer Vision opportunities, including AI feasibility assessment and camera placement strategy.
Designed an internal AI-native solutioning operating system (Claude + Obsidian) that cut proposal first drafts from 2-3 hours to 5-10 minutes.
Led WorkOS, an agentic enterprise operating system unifying role-based access, onboarding and cross-tool integrations.
Building this portfolio's voice agent with tool calling grounded in structured data.

SignalRoom: a LangGraph workflow where code verifies every model quote against a numbered transcript line, numbers are classified by provenance, and human approval is a real interrupt rather than a button.

Cochlea: a local MCP server that measures a sung take so an LLM coaches from cited numbers. Its pitch tracker was picked on a benchmark (SwiftF0, 95.2% within 50 cents vs pYIN's 92.7% on vocadito), and a planted-defect eval finds 7 of 7.
Owned discovery, feasibility, architecture and deployment planning for 12 concurrent enterprise PoCs, authoring every Solution Architecture Specification.
Fixed a failed on-site Raspberry Pi + relay automation setup during a PoC by redrawing the wiring on customer premises.
After one site turned up 10 cameras on 3 resolutions, made a signed camera spec sheet part of every architecture spec.
Ran a 10-camera highway-safety PoC across a 165km corridor on on-prem edge hardware, with a path to ~100 cameras.
SignalRoom encodes the discovery-to-brief work as a system: requirements, open items and contradictions carry the line the customer said them on, and unknowns stay open instead of being filled in.
Translated an ambiguous early-stage vision into two shipped products at Project Dark Horse, directing roadmap and delivery cadence.

ReadTrail's product vision separates decisions made, open questions and non-goals, documents planned work separately from shipped work, and says plainly that nobody outside the project has used it yet.
Turned field findings into product priorities with Product and Engineering through a capability-gap register at HawkVision.
Part of the HawkVision team that was runner-up for Product Excellence (startup category) at the ISPMA SPM Summit 2026, IIM Bangalore.
Built HawkVision's initial India sales pipeline from scratch.
Stood up a 3-person solutioning team in a month at the CEO's request: every request got an owner, a first response within 2 working days and a proposal draft within 5.
Authored 10+ RFI/RFP responses across automotive, fabrication, construction, oil & gas and energy, each scoped at 1,000+ cameras.
Supported the CEO on international business development and partnerships.
B.A. in Economics and Political Science from the University of Delhi: analytical thinking, incentives, institutions, human systems.
Customer discovery and solutioning work depends on reading how organizations actually behave, not only what the RFP says.

faq.q: Is he primarily technical or business?
faq.a: He's moved across both. He started by building software, later worked directly on enterprise AI deployments, and took on broader solutioning and business responsibility, ending as Head of Global Solutions and Head of India Sales. Since leaving in August 2026 he has been building again, in public, and he's available immediately.

faq.q: How did he get into coding without a CS degree?
faq.a: He studied Economics and Political Science at Delhi University (2019 to 2022), then did the Coding Ninjas Full Stack Web Development job bootcamp (2022 to 2023), and learned the rest through projects and professional work: an SDE internship at Edviron, leading a small team at Project Dark Horse, and engineering at HawkVision.

faq.q: What connects economics and engineering for him?
faq.a: Both are about systems: incentives, constraints, and how parts interact. Economics and political science taught him to think about human systems and institutions; engineering gave him the tools to build technical systems. Solutioning work sits right between the two.

faq.q: What is he building right now?
faq.a: SignalRoom, a workflow that turns a discovery call transcript into a solution brief where every claim is tied to a line the customer actually said, with its evaluation and its failures published; the latest change is a code check that keeps a figure one speaker corrects on the next line as a dispute. Also ReadTrail, a privacy-first Chrome reading companion that is a working MVP (2.0 on GitHub, not yet on the Chrome Web Store), and this portfolio, a voice-capable AI agent grounded in structured profile data. On the side: Cochlea, a local MCP server that measures a sung take so an LLM can coach from the numbers, heading toward a coach for beginner singers; Spotify Mood Curator, a working playlist builder on real listening data; and Atlas, a personal capture pipeline. He's between roles and available immediately.
